assertions.anchor: don't guess which one is wanted if the request is ambiguous, ask
assertions.why: running the wrong mode edits the wrong things
structural: the downward pair is documented before Close

assertions.anchor: route: apply the three questions from
assertions.why: re-anchored for #25 (was the single routing question): Route applies the three questions, and they are the reason for every class call

assertions.anchor: count the yeses: 3 → pathfinder, 2 → navigator, 1 → builder,
assertions.why: the class is a count of yeses (AND, not OR), not a judgment call

assertions.anchor: then apply the veto: irreversible (q2) and unverifiable (q3) → pathfinder, whatever the count
assertions.why: the method's worst case: the wrong version reads like the right one and cannot be taken back; without the veto a familiar irreversible migration scores navigator

assertions.anchor: dispatch: re-score before writing anything down
assertions.why: re-score at every boundary: a decision made or spec written is what lets the class drop; without re-scoring, tier inertia

assertions.anchor: both go in the spend line
assertions.why: Mode B records the class planned at Route and the class it ran as after re-scoring, so the ledger shows where tier inertia or escalation happened

assertions.anchor: route down only as far as the project's gates reach
assertions.why: the verification axis: work with no cheap gate routes up however mechanical it looks
'Decisions already made' is the whole point of a handoff; an empty one must block, not be papered over

assertions.anchor: no section left as the template's angle-bracket placeholder text
assertions.why: a placeholder spec forces the receiving tier to re-derive, which is the cost the handoff exists to avoid

assertions.anchor: say so inline, plainly, before proceeding
assertions.why: a mis-tiered session flagged only in a later report has already spent the budget
W4 escalation rule: grinding down-tier burns savings invisibly

assertions.anchor: gates catch defective output, not expensive output
assertions.why: the reason early return must be a rule: nothing else catches it

assertions.anchor: one level up and never further
assertions.why: artifacts climb one cycle level at a time

assertions.anchor: never assert savings against an unmeasured baseline
assertions.why: spend-ledger never-claim rule: the ledger records, it does not advertise

assertions.anchor: never quote the ratio without its price-table date and token-volume assumption

assertions.why: re-assessment is reserved for an empty queue or a wrong-feeling frame, not folded into a routine close

assertions.anchor: never invent a lane, a decision, or a gap
quote the three questions verbatim when applying them
assertions.why: re-anchored for #25 (was: the routing test): softened questions stop cutting against the reach-for-the-best-model instinct
